content: The text discusses the impact of increasing the number of elements on the time taken for a sorting process. As the size of the dataset being sorted increases, the computation time also extends significantly. When discussing computation time in algorithm analysis, it is standard to characterize time as a function of the input size, allowing for better understanding and prediction of algorithm behavior with larger inputs. Furthermore, the text emphasizes the importance of providing upper bounds on running time rather than lower bounds. Providing an upper limit (e.g., the program will not run for more than three seconds) offers a reliable performance guarantee to users, which is particularly useful in real-time applications, unlike a lower limit which offers no practical assurance on the maximum duration a program might take.
